column1: # Sumner's DISCLOSED editorial interventions in the 1825 text.
# WHAT THIS IS: every place where Sumner himself, in a footnote, tells the reader that what he
# printed differs from the manuscript. These are his own admissions, harvested from the plates as
# the volume run reads them. Primary evidence, free, and not anticipated by PLAN §6.4, which
# listed only Campbell/Corns/Hale/Tweedie and the 1825 facsimile plates as sources.
# WHAT THIS IS NOT: a list of everywhere the 1825 departs from SP 9/61. Sumner normalised
# silently and at scale (PLAN §4a). This file records only what he ADMITTED. Never present it as
# a complete collation — the undisclosed changes are the larger and more dangerous set.
# Ruled 2026-08-04 (Wilson): harvest as we go; feeds PLAN §6.4 at M4.
# SCOPE RULED 2026-08-04 (Wilson), CONVENTIONS §5a: this file holds TEXTUAL notes only — the ones
# where Sumner admits the manuscript differs from what he printed, or that he changed something.
# SCHOLARLY Latin notes (Sumner assembling authorities, glossing an allusion, defending Milton)
# are transcribed in the chunk's ## apparatus-sumner-la and get NO row here. When in doubt, do not
# ledger it. This file answers exactly one question — where did Sumner admit changing the text? —
# and a page of Reformed proof-texts filed as an "intervention" would corrupt that answer.
# Deliberately NOT ledgered so far:
#   II.vii, La p. 454, [^la4] — scholarly. Bucer/Calvin/Ursinus/Gomarus for Milton on the Sabbath,
#   Peter Martyr against, Musculus last. Hinge: 'Omnes hactenus cum Miltono faciunt.'
# LAYER COLUMN ADDED 2026-08-28, from I.ii. The file was built assuming textual notes are a
# Latin-volume phenomenon and its page column was called `la_page`. En 20's note 7 disproves that:
# it is a textual note printed in the ENGLISH volume, where Sumner says the manuscript's next
# clause was "incorrectly transcribed" and states what he rendered instead. The truer rule is that
# Sumner puts a textual note wherever his reader needs it — in the Latin volume when the Latin is
# doubtful, in the English when the doubt changed his translation. `layer` is `la` or `en-sumner`
# and `page` is that volume's printed page. CONVENTIONS §5a's two-kind classification is unchanged;
# only the assumption about which volume carries such notes was wrong.
# kind vocabulary (extend as needed, don't invent synonyms):
#   word-order   Sumner rearranged Milton's words
#   emendation   Sumner changed a reading
#   supplement   Sumner supplied something absent from the MS
#   ms-state     Sumner reports damage, a gap, or a hand-change without changing the text
#   uncertain    Sumner flags the MS reading as doubtful

column7: MS word order differs from the printed text; Sumner reordered the clause about Matt. v. 33 / Jacob. v. 12 so that "per Deum jurare non prohibemur" follows the Matthew citation rather than the James one.
column8: Quo melius ratio grammatica servaretur, ordinem leviter mutavi — to preserve the grammar.

column7: Sumner flags the MS reading `qualis ipse est` as doubtful and asks whether `se` should be read — i.e. whether Milton wrote that God wills to be conceived as he IS, or as he PRESENTS HIMSELF. The text is printed unchanged.
column8: Sic in MS. An legendum se? — the MS reads thus; query the reading.

column7: Sumner flags `SUMME BEATUS` (most blessed) as the MS reading and asks whether `benignus` (most gracious) should be read, on the ground of the context and the texts cited. The Latin is printed unchanged — but he then TRANSLATED the emendation: En 28 reads "He is MOST GRACIOUS", with no English note. Printed the MS in one layer, adopted the conjecture in the other.
column8: Sic in MS. Sed vide an legendum benignus, quod et contextus, et loci citati postulare videntur — context and the cited passages seem to require it.

column7: The ledger's FIRST English-volume row. On Exod. iii. 14 Sumner quotes the manuscript verbatim, judges the clause after `Ehie qui sum vel ero` to have been incorrectly transcribed, and states the reconstruction he translated from (`et si persona prima in tertiam affinis verbi mutatur, Jave, qui est vel erit`), citing Simon's Hebrew Lexicon, Buxtorf and Cappellus. The Latin volume prints the MS clause with no note at all, so this admission exists in the English layer only.
column8: conceiving the next clause to have been incorrectly transcribed, I have rendered it as if it had been written—
